observations.observation: Kingsbridge built up with a 2-3-2-3 shape, using a left-back who inverted inside 34% of the time, forming a 3-2 box for protection against counters.
observations.consequence: This formation improved defensive cover centrally but shifted width responsibility to the wingers.
observations.coachAction: Opponents should have their winger track inside or accept the 3-2 and press centre-backs.

observations.observation: Kingsbridge attacked evenly, with 32% down left flank, 34% centre, and 34% right; after a substitution, attacks down the right fell from 48% to 26%, shifting play focus.
observations.consequence: The attack became less balanced, reducing threats from the right flank later in the match.
observations.coachAction: Shift defensive focus away from the weakened flank and prepare for overloads on the opposite side.

observations.observation: Kingsbridge's defensive block dropped from 37 m to 30 m from goal after a substitution, moving their block deeper in later stages.
observations.consequence: The deeper block reduces space behind defenders but concedes more territory to the opponent.
observations.coachAction: Use width, patience, and set pieces to break down this deeper defense.

observations.observation: Northgate built out mainly with their 6 dropping between centre-backs in 58% of phases, forming a back three to counter a two-striker press, at the cost of midfield presence.
observations.consequence: This provided clean first passes but weakened midfield control in front of the defense, inviting mid-block pressure.

observations.observation: At 61 minutes, Northgate switched formation from 4-3-3 to 4-4-2 and moved their last defensive line deeper from 26 m to 20 m, adopting a lower defensive block.
observations.consequence: This change decreased space behind the defense, reducing vulnerability to through balls but conceding midfield territory.
observations.coachAction: Respond by increasing midfield control and adjust to fewer spaces behind the defense for through balls.
